faq.q: How much is a house in Halkidiki?
faq.a: It depends on the area, the size, the age and above all the distance to the sea. Houses in popular parts of Kassandra and near the best beaches cost more, while village houses inland are usually more affordable. Use the price filter to see what fits your budget.

faq.q: Can I buy a house in Halkidiki and live there all year?
faq.a: Yes, if you choose the right house and area. Check heating, insulation and winter access, and prefer a town with year-round services such as Nea Moudania or Polygyros. Non-EU citizens also need a residence permit to live in Greece. Many owners in these towns live here all year.

faq.q: Which part of Halkidiki is best for a family home?
faq.a: Families living here all year often choose Nea Propontida or the area around Polygyros, for schools, shops and the shorter drive to Thessaloniki. For holiday family homes, Kassandra and Sithonia offer more beaches and summer activities. We can show you options in several areas in one trip.

faq.q: Do houses in Halkidiki come with a garden or pool?
faq.a: Many do. Detached houses and maisonettes usually have a garden or yard, and some larger homes have a private pool. Each listing shows the outdoor features, and you can filter for them. Apartments in small complexes may also share a pool with neighbours.

body:
Homes for sale in Halkidiki by area

Kassandra offers the most choice and the shortest drive from Thessaloniki. Sithonia has homes among pine forests and quiet coves. Nea Propontida and Polygyros suit buyers who want towns that stay busy all year, and Aristotelis offers a more local life in the north-east.

Houses near the beach in Halkidiki

Many Halkidiki homes for sale are within walking distance of the sea. A house on the first line costs more than one a few streets back, so decide how close you really need to be.

Family homes for year-round living

If you plan to live here all year, look at heating, insulation and winter road access. Larger towns such as Nea Moudania and Polygyros have schools, shops and health services, while smaller resort villages can be very quiet from autumn to spring.

Holiday homes in Halkidiki

For holidays, location and outdoor space matter most: a terrace, a garden, maybe a pool. Think about who will look after the house while you are away; we offer property management after the purchase.

Buying a house in Greece: steps and costs

Before you buy, your lawyer and an engineer check the title, the building permit, any legalisation of extra spaces and the energy certificate. As of November 2026, to be confirmed by our lawyer, transfer tax on a resale is 3.09%, VAT on new builds is suspended until 31/12/2026, and other fees typically add several percent. Our buying guide covers each step.
